findings.title: NetFx handshake-failure handling depends on HTTP status and headers that ClientWebSocket does not expose
findings.evidence: "HTTP 401 Unauthorized ... Add-in surfaces a UI error"; "HTTP 429 Too Many Requests ... Add-in backs off per the `Retry-After` response header"; "WebSocketException with HTTP 401 → ... HTTP 400 → ... HTTP 429 → back off per `Retry-After` header."
findings.problem: The add-in runtime is .NET Framework 4.8 `ClientWebSocket`, but the spec requires the client to branch on pre-upgrade HTTP 400/401/429 and read `Retry-After`. That information is not reliably available from failed `ConnectAsync` calls on the target client API.
findings.why_it_matters: Auth failure UX, lockout behavior, and retry/backoff policy cannot be implemented or tested as written on the stated client runtime.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace this with a client-observable contract supported on .NET Framework 4.8, or add a separate HTTPS preflight endpoint that returns status and headers the add-in can read before opening the WebSocket.

findings.title: GetFeatureTree service contract requires a `compressed` choice that the wire protocol never sends
findings.evidence: "IReadOnlyList<FeatureNode> GetFeatureTree(bool includeSuppressed, bool compressed);" versus "public record GetFeatureTreeInput : IToolInput { public bool IncludeSuppressed { get; init; } = false; }"
findings.problem: The adapter contract needs the caller to specify `compressed`, but the cross-process input DTO has no corresponding field and no normative default is defined.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementers must guess whether the tool returns compressed or full trees, which changes payload size, hashes, viewer output, and downstream agent behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Either add `Compressed` to `GetFeatureTreeInput` and specify its semantics, or remove the `compressed` parameter from the adapter interface and hard-code one documented behavior.

findings.title: Oversize screenshot fallback contradicts the `StateSnapshot.FeatureTreeHash` invariant
findings.evidence: SPEC-02: "The resulting `ToolResultMessage` substitutes a placeholder `StateAfter` ... `FeatureTreeHash = \"OVERSIZE\"`". SPEC-01: "The `FeatureTreeHash` MUST still reflect the hash of the complete (non-truncated) tree".
findings.problem: The fallback error path instructs the add-in to emit a sentinel hash value that SPEC-01 explicitly forbids for truncated live-document state.
findings.why_it_matters: This message cannot satisfy both specs simultaneously; validators, hash checks, and any consumer relying on `FeatureTreeHash` will diverge.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the real full-tree hash in the oversize error path, or formally extend SPEC-01 with an explicit oversize sentinel contract and update validators/hash logic accordingly.

findings.title: Critical decoration-persistence behavior was moved to SPEC-05 but its interface is still undefined
findings.evidence: "SPEC-05 §X (TBD — to be authored in the next spec-authoring pass) will define the `DhfDecorationPersister` contract in detail."
findings.problem: Citation durability, retry, circuit breaker, and `LockSessionAsync` escalation now depend on a component whose API and failure contract do not exist in the spec set.
findings.why_it_matters: SPEC-07 and SPEC-04 cannot be integrated, tested, or failure-injected consistently without inventing behavior in implementation.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the persister contract now: method signatures, required inputs (`entryId`, `sessionId`, payload), retry policy, circuit-breaker thresholds, lock escalation conditions, and returned failure types.

findings.title: SPEC-07 still requires `DecorationWriteMs` in `PipelineResult` after moving decoration writes out of SPEC-07
findings.evidence: §3.2: "decoration INSERT is SPEC-05's budget". §6.4: "public sealed record StageLatencies { ... public required int DecorationWriteMs { get; init; } ... }"
findings.problem: The pipeline result requires a latency field for work SPEC-07 no longer performs or observes.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementations must either fabricate a value or block on out-of-module behavior, which breaks metric integrity and contract clarity.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove `DecorationWriteMs` from SPEC-07 `StageLatencies`, or explicitly redefine it as a SPEC-05-populated field outside `PipelineResult`.

findings.title: Viewer raw-input gating relies on `ViewerOptions.VocabRawInputAllowed`, but that option is not defined in the config surface
findings.evidence: SDR-06-008: "`ViewerOptions.VocabRawInputAllowed`"; §3 code block: "public sealed class ViewerOptions { public bool EnableStretchEndpoints { get; init; } }"; §13 config only shows `enableStretchEndpoints`.
findings.problem: The security-sensitive switch controlling raw utterance and `ParsedIntent` exposure exists in prose only; no actual option or configuration key is defined.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementations will either hard-code the behavior or invent their own config shape, creating inconsistent and potentially unsafe exposure of sensitive input.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `VocabRawInputAllowed` to `ViewerOptions`, add its config key to §13, and specify the per-tenant override source and default behavior.

top_3_must_fix: Define the missing SPEC-05 decoration persistence contract referenced by SPEC-07 SDR-07-012.
Replace or redesign the pre-upgrade HTTP 400/401/429 handling contract so it is observable from .NET Framework 4.8 `ClientWebSocket`.
Reconcile the `GetFeatureTree` API mismatch by adding or removing the missing `compressed` parameter in the wire contract.
